doc.title: Ruth Lion interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998

chapter: Becoming a jazz fan and DJ
title: Discovering jazz through her mother's Victrola
summary: Rowe asks how she became a fan; she recalls her mother's music school and dancing to Ellington's 'Blue Bubbles' on a 78 at age six.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: You couldn’t do any better than to listen to Thelonious. It seems like sometimes the simplest things are the best, you know. And I think these gentlemen certainly understood that to some extent. I would like to ask you, before we get to Alfred and his vision of Blue Note Records, you must have been a jazz fan before you met him. Is that right?
How did you come to love jazz?

Actually through my mother, who had the first African-American school of music in the United States, The Hansbury School of Music. And we had early wind-up Victrolas. My mother of course was in classical music, but she was not against jazz or any popular music. And with this wind-up Victrola my brother and I, I was six years of age, heard an Ellington, one of those, you know, it was “Blue Bubbles.” And we just danced, and we were just so happy with that music. And I think I’ve been a jazz fan ever since then.
Really touched something in you, huh?
Were those 78s at that time? Or was it a ten inch?
